doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

title: Mustaches as protest at West Point
summary: Band members grew mustaches as a small protest against Vietnam and the draft until a surprise inspection.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I understand that you and some of your mates grew mustaches as a mild form of protest?

Yeah we did. You’ve got to remember, in that era, you know that many young people did not think it was a good thing what we were doing in Vietnam. And also it was the idea of the draft and there was a lot going on and a lot of protests and marches and all kinds of stuff. And we kind of felt a little strange because we had real short haircuts and everybody else had long hair so immediately they know if we were in an area around West Point you know the surrounding area by twenty miles, they knew we were in the Army you know. So anyway yeah, you could have facial — well not a beard there. Maybe you could do it in the Navy but at that time you could only have mustaches. So we grew mustaches. And after a while the career people started thinking why are all these young guys growing mustaches? And you know they had to be trimmed a certain way, you couldn’t go any longer than this and you certainly couldn’t go down at all you know, it had to be — so yeah we had a surprise mustache inspection one day. We all had to go down and trim them up you know. But it was just our little thing of trying to, you know, say we’re individuals.
Well I’m glad your second trip overseas was not to go be in a war.
